newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment rises to 10.0 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment rises to 10.0 pct in Oct.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate rose to 10.0 percent in October from 9.9 percent in September.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.7 percent in October.
Full time employment rose by 44,000 from the month before, while part time employment remained unchanged.
Statistics Canada said the labor force grew faster than employment in October. As a result, the number of people looking for work rose by 16,000 and the unemployment rate edged up.
All of the employment gains in October were in the private sector. The self-employed accounted for two-thirds of the gains, while the number of employees rose only 16,000.
Employment in construction rose 17,000 in October, in line with recent declines in mortgage rates and growth in housing starts.
Employment in finance, insurance and real estate rose 12,000 in October, bringing gains over the past two months to 32,000.
However, manufacturing employment fell by 30,000 in October, after growing by 108,000 in the previuos six months. The decrease follows a decline in manufacturers' shipments in August.
Almost all employment gains were among adults, aged 25 or over. Adult employment has grown by 168,000 since the beginning of the year.
